conclusion: Random visual dropout becomes strongly harmful near 30 percent and above on the tested trajectory.
Short visual outages are strongly timing-dependent; local metrics expose failures hidden by global RMSE.
Online temporal calibration keeps every tested signed offset below one metre RMSE.
Disabling temporal calibration causes catastrophic divergence for every nonzero tested offset.
Trace diagnostics confirm broad persistent failure, not isolated outliers, in all fixed-offset cases.
Ten-times IMU degradation raises RMSE and NEES but does not cross the one-metre service threshold.
